gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's maker-store prices for the UST ALR floor-rising screens, which start at $999 (NothingProjector PET Crystal Classic, 85% ALR) and $1,102 (VIVIDSTORM S PRO Classic, US-stock Arizona clearance), well under the $1,649 to $2,100 cards ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: I compared four pages. projector-screen-guide.com (updated 2026-11-09) gives no prices, only 'Check price on Amazon' links. primeareviews.com gives only the tiers '$500 and up' and '$200 to $500', with no check date. projectorverdict.com's motorized guide has dated S PRO prices from 2026-11-05 ($1,962 for 100", $2,080 for 110", $2,359 for 120") and the Kestrel TT3 at $1,923, but it lists only those two floor-risers. It does not mention the NothingProjector Classic or Black Series, the NexiGo, VIVIDSTORM's Arizona clearance S PRO, or the long-throw S ALR. None of the pages puts the whole category side by side at today's maker prices.
decides: For a UST shopper, the cheapest maker-sold floor-rising ALR screens today are the NothingProjector Classic (from $999) and the VIVIDSTORM S PRO Classic from Arizona US stock (from $1,102). ChatGPT's NexiGo ($1,899) and S PRO P ($2,100) cards are the expensive end. The NothingProjector Black Series 120" at $1,799 undercuts the NexiGo 120" at $1,899. For a standard-throw projector, the NothingProjector Matte White ($699, 1.3 gain, long, short or UST throw) and the VIVIDSTORM S ALR long-throw (from $1,194) are the choices. Every UST screen in this list loses for a ceiling projector. One caveat: the store search returns each listing's lowest variant price. I could not open the per-size variants because every store returned HTTP 429, so '$999 for 120"' is not established.
